repair_fixes.steps: 1. Unplug the VSS connector and check for corrosion or bent pins • 2. Clean contacts with electrical contact cleaner • 3. Replace a damaged pigtail with a soldered, heat-shrunk splice • 4. Verify a clean speed trace on a scan tool at a slow roll

repair_fixes.steps: 1. Disconnect the battery negative terminal • 2. Remove the sensor retaining bolt and pull the sensor from its bore • 3. Install the new sensor with a fresh O-ring seated fully • 4. Clear the code and confirm speedometer/cruise operation on a test drive

repair_fixes.steps: 1. Back-probe signal, reference, and ground at the ECM connector • 2. Trace the harness for chafe points near the transmission or subframe • 3. Repair with proper gauge wire and abrasion-resistant loom • 4. Road test through the full speed range while monitoring signal quality

repair_fixes.steps: 1. Inspect engine-to-body and battery-to-chassis ground straps for corrosion • 2. Clean or replace corroded straps and terminals • 3. Verify voltage drop across each strap is under 0.2V while cranking • 4. Clear the code and retest

repair_fixes.steps: 1. Disconnect the battery negative terminal • 2. Remove the sensor from the transmission case, noting fluid loss • 3. Install the new sensor with a fresh O-ring • 4. Top off fluid, clear the code, and verify signal on a scan tool

repair_fixes.title: Check transmission fluid level and filter condition
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Check fluid level and condition • 2. Change fluid and filter, since debris is the most common cause of a sticking shift solenoid • 3. Clear the code and drive-cycle through all gears • 4. Monitor for the code returning

repair_fixes.title: Command the named shift solenoid with a scan-tool actuator test
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Connect a scan tool with bi-directional solenoid control • 2. Command the named shift solenoid on and off • 3. Confirm line pressure or shift-quality PID responds to the command • 4. No response isolates the fault to that solenoid or its valve-body connector before condemning the whole pack

repair_fixes.title: Test and replace the named shift solenoid
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Test the named solenoid's resistance against spec • 2. Command it individually with a scan tool and listen/feel for a click and gear response • 3. Replace the solenoid, typically as part of the valve-body solenoid pack • 4. Clear the code and verify normal shifting

repair_fixes.title: Repair shift solenoid wiring at the valve body connector
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Remove the valve body pan for access to the internal connector • 2. Inspect for corrosion or a broken pin at the solenoid connector • 3. Repair or replace the connector/harness section • 4. Refill fluid, clear the code, and verify commanded shifts

repair_fixes.title: Complete the manufacturer drive cycle
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Confirm no other DTCs are stored - address any real faults first • 2. Drive the manufacturer's specified drive cycle (typically a cold start, mixed city and 55 mph steady-state segments) • 3. Re-scan and confirm all readiness monitors report Complete

repair_fixes.title: Complete the manufacturer drive cycle
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Confirm no other DTCs are stored - address any real faults first • 2. Drive the manufacturer's specified drive cycle (typically a cold start, mixed city and 55 mph steady-state segments) • 3. Re-scan and confirm all readiness monitors report Complete

repair_fixes.title: Verify battery and charging health before the drive cycle
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Test battery resting voltage (12.4V+) and charging voltage (13.5-14.7V) • 2. A weak battery resets monitors and prevents completion • 3. Recharge or replace the battery before repeating the drive cycle

repair_fixes.title: Verify battery and charging health before the drive cycle
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Test battery resting voltage (12.4V+) and charging voltage (13.5-14.7V) • 2. A weak battery resets monitors and prevents completion • 3. Recharge or replace the battery before repeating the drive cycle

repair_fixes.title: Diagnose a monitor that never completes
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Identify which monitor stays incomplete on a capable scan tool • 2. Check the enabling criteria for that monitor (fuel level, ambient temperature, trip requirements) • 3. Pinpoint-test the sensors that gate the monitor per service information

repair_fixes.title: Diagnose a monitor that never completes
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Identify which monitor stays incomplete on a capable scan tool • 2. Check the enabling criteria for that monitor (fuel level, ambient temperature, trip requirements) • 3. Pinpoint-test the sensors that gate the monitor per service information

repair_fixes.title: Smoke-test intake for vacuum/air leaks
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Connect a smoke machine to the intake at idle • 2. Watch for smoke escaping at intake gaskets, PCV hoses, or brake booster line • 3. Replace any leaking gasket or hose • 4. Clear codes and verify fuel trims return toward 0%

repair_fixes.title: Replace fuel filter and test fuel pump output
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Replace the fuel filter if serviceable • 2. Measure fuel pump pressure and volume against spec under load • 3. Replace a weak pump if it fails the test • 4. Clear codes and confirm rail pressure holds steady

repair_fixes.title: Inspect and repair exhaust manifold gasket leak
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Inspect the exhaust manifold gasket and studs near the upstream O2 sensor for leaks • 2. Replace the gasket and any corroded studs • 3. Torque to spec in sequence • 4. Clear codes and re-verify trim correction

repair_fixes.title: Clean MAF sensor and inspect for false-high airflow readings
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Remove the MAF sensor and inspect the hot-wire element for contamination • 2. Clean with dedicated MAF cleaner (never touch the element) • 3. Reinstall and clear codes • 4. Compare live MAF g/s reading against expected values

repair_fixes.title: Test fuel injectors for leakage and replace as needed
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Perform a fuel injector leak-down/drip test • 2. Identify any injector leaking past its seat • 3. Replace the faulty injector(s) and seals • 4. Clear codes and verify trims return toward 0%

repair_fixes.title: Replace stuck-open fuel pressure regulator
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Depressurize the fuel system • 2. Remove the regulator and inspect the diaphragm/valve for sticking • 3. Install the replacement regulator with new seals • 4. Clear codes and confirm rail pressure holds at commanded target

repair_fixes.title: Clear debris from the barometric sensor sampling port
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Locate the external BARO sensor and its atmospheric sampling port • 2. Clear dust or insect debris blocking the port opening • 3. Reseat the connector while there • 4. Clear the code and compare the reading against local ambient pressure

repair_fixes.title: Replace the external barometric pressure sensor
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Verify the reading is frozen or offset against a known ambient pressure at key-on • 2. Unplug and unbolt the sensor from its mounting • 3. Install the replacement and reconnect • 4. Confirm the new reading matches ambient and tracks altitude changes

repair_fixes.title: Repair BARO sensor reference or signal wiring
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Back-probe the connector and verify 5V reference, signal, and ground • 2. Trace and repair any damaged conductor between sensor and ECM • 3. Verify a clean, ambient-plausible signal after repair • 4. Clear the code and monitor across several key cycles

repair_fixes.title: Replace the ECM housing an internal BARO sensor
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Confirm the platform integrates the BARO sensor inside the ECM and no external sensor exists • 2. Rule out connector and supply faults at the ECM first • 3. Install and program the replacement module per the manufacturer's security procedure • 4. Verify the internal sensor now reads ambient correctly

repair_fixes.title: Inspect for vacuum leaks and check fuel trim data with a scan tool
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Review short- and long-term fuel trim values by bank on a scan tool • 2. Smoke-test the intake for leaks matching the trending bank • 3. Repair any leak found • 4. Clear codes and recheck trims after a drive cycle

repair_fixes.title: Clean throttle body and check MAF/MAP sensor readings
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Clean the throttle body bore and blade of carbon buildup • 2. Compare MAF/MAP readings against expected values at idle and 2,500 RPM • 3. Address any sensor reading found out of spec • 4. Clear codes and monitor trim recovery

repair_fixes.title: Diagnose fuel delivery imbalance affecting one bank
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Compare fuel pressure and injector pulse width between banks • 2. Identify a restricted injector, filter sock, or fuel rail issue isolated to one bank • 3. Repair or replace the faulted component • 4. Clear codes and confirm trims converge between banks

repair_fixes.title: Inspect for contamination sources (oil, coolant, silicone) reaching the exhaust
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Check for oil consumption, coolant leaks, or recent use of silicone sealant near the intake/exhaust • 2. Repair the contamination source if found • 3. Inspect the sensor tip for a sooty or white/gray glassy coating • 4. Clear codes after addressing the source

repair_fixes.title: Replace slow-responding oxygen sensor
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Identify the affected bank/sensor position • 2. Remove with an O2 sensor socket and inspect the old sensor tip for contamination • 3. Apply anti-seize and install the new sensor • 4. Clear codes and verify switching frequency improves

repair_fixes.title: Repair exhaust leak diluting sensor sample
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Smoke-test the exhaust system upstream of the affected sensor • 2. Replace leaking gaskets or cracked pipe sections • 3. Torque fasteners to spec • 4. Clear codes and re-verify switching speed

repair_fixes.title: Test O2 sensor heater circuit fuse and relay
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Locate the O2 heater fuse and relay in the underhood fuse box • 2. Inspect and test with a multimeter for continuity and proper switching • 3. Replace any blown fuse or failed relay • 4. Clear codes and verify heater current draw

repair_fixes.title: Replace oxygen sensor with failed heater
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Identify the affected bank/sensor position from the code • 2. Unplug the connector and remove the sensor with an O2 sensor socket • 3. Apply anti-seize to threads (avoid the sensor tip) and install the new sensor • 4. Reconnect and clear codes

repair_fixes.title: Repair O2 heater circuit wiring
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Measure heater element resistance at the connector against spec • 2. Voltage-drop test the heater supply and ground legs • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring near the exhaust manifold with high-temp splices • 4. Confirm heater current draw matches spec

repair_fixes.title: Check engine oil level and condition
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Check engine oil level on the dipstick with the engine off and cold • 2. Inspect oil color and consistency for sludge or fuel dilution • 3. Top up or perform a full oil and filter change with the specified viscosity • 4. Clear the code and verify VTEC engagement returns at the commanded RPM

repair_fixes.title: Test the VTEC oil pressure switch
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Locate the VTEC oil pressure switch on the cylinder head • 2. Back-probe the switch connector and confirm it opens/closes with engine oil pressure • 3. Replace the switch if it stays open or closed regardless of pressure • 4. Clear the code and confirm the switch now toggles during a test drive

repair_fixes.title: Clean the VTEC oil strainer and test the spool valve solenoid
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Remove the spool valve assembly and its inline oil strainer screen • 2. Clean or replace a screen clogged with sludge or metal debris • 3. Measure spool valve solenoid coil resistance against the factory specification • 4. Command the solenoid with a scan tool and confirm it clicks and moves freely • 5. Reinstall with a new gasket and road-test for clean VTEC engagement

repair_fixes.title: Repair PCM wiring to the VTEC solenoid and pressure switch
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Inspect the harness and connectors between the PCM and both VTEC components • 2. Test each circuit for continuity, shorts to ground, and shorts to power • 3. Repair or replace chafed wiring or a corroded connector pin • 4. Clear the code and confirm the PCM data list shows correct switch/solenoid activity

repair_fixes.title: Inspect and reseat the ignition coil connector
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Unplug the connector for the affected coil letter/cylinder • 2. Inspect pins for corrosion, heat damage, or a bent terminal • 3. Clean contacts with electrical contact cleaner and reseat fully • 4. Clear the code and re-test under load

repair_fixes.title: Replace the ignition coil
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Remove the engine cover and any coil retaining bolts • 2. Disconnect the harness and pull the coil from its plug well • 3. Install the replacement coil and torque the retaining bolt to spec • 4. Reconnect, clear the code, and verify no misfire returns

repair_fixes.title: Repair coil driver wiring back to the ECM/ignition module
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Measure coil primary resistance at the connector against spec • 2. Voltage-drop test the driver, ground, and reference legs to the ECM or ignition control module • 3. Repair chafed or corroded conductors with soldered, heat-shrunk splices • 4. Clear codes and confirm clean coil-on/coil-off waveforms with a scope

repair_fixes.title: Replace a failed ignition control/driver module
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Confirm coil and wiring test good but the driver circuit still faults • 2. Locate the ignition control module or driver stage (stand-alone or integrated in the ECM) • 3. Replace the module and reprogram/relearn as required • 4. Clear codes and verify all coil channels fire correctly

repair_fixes.title: Inspect and replace crankshaft/camshaft position sensor
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Identify which sensor the correlation fault points to on the scan tool freeze frame • 2. Unplug and remove the affected position sensor • 3. Inspect the reluctor wheel/tone ring for chips or debris • 4. Install the new sensor with correct air-gap shim and clear codes

repair_fixes.title: Inspect timing chain/belt for stretch or jumped timing
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Remove the timing cover and verify cam-to-crank alignment against factory timing marks • 2. Measure chain stretch or check belt tooth wear • 3. Replace the timing chain/belt, tensioner, and guides as a set • 4. Reset timing to factory marks and verify correlation with a scan tool

repair_fixes.title: Repair crank/cam sensor wiring and connectors
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Back-probe the sensor signal and ground at each connector while cranking • 2. Voltage-drop test the harness runs back to the ECM • 3. Repair chafed conductors near the timing cover with heat-shrink splices • 4. Confirm clean square-wave signals on a scope

repair_fixes.title: Inspect and reseat the ignition coil connector
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Unplug the connector for the affected coil letter/cylinder • 2. Inspect pins for corrosion, heat damage, or a bent terminal • 3. Clean contacts with electrical contact cleaner and reseat fully • 4. Clear the code and re-test under load

repair_fixes.title: Replace the ignition coil

repair_fixes.title: Repair coil driver wiring back to the ECM/ignition module
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Measure coil primary resistance at the connector against spec • 2. Voltage-drop test the driver, ground, and reference legs to the ECM or ignition control module • 3. Repair chafed or corroded conductors with soldered, heat-shrunk splices • 4. Clear codes and confirm clean coil-on/coil-off waveforms with a scope

repair_fixes.title: Replace a failed ignition control/driver module
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Confirm coil and wiring test good but the driver circuit still faults • 2. Locate the ignition control module or driver stage (stand-alone or integrated in the ECM) • 3. Replace the module and reprogram/relearn as required • 4. Clear codes and verify all coil channels fire correctly

repair_fixes.title: Identify the theft-deterrent generation and run the manufacturer relearn procedure
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Determine whether the vehicle uses VATS/PASS-Key (resistor pellet key, roughly 1986-1996) or Passlock/PASS-Key III (plain or transponder key, no pellet, roughly 1996-on) from its model year and RPO code • 2. With the key in the ignition, turn to RUN and leave it there without cranking through the full theft-deterrent lamp cycle (commonly about 10 minutes) • 3. Turn the key OFF, then back to RUN or START to attempt a normal start • 4. Repeat the wait-and-start sequence up to three times if the first attempt does not succeed • 5. If the vehicle starts and stays running, no further theft-deterrent diagnosis is needed

repair_fixes.title: Test the VATS key pellet and clean the decoder-ring contacts (VATS-equipped vehicles only)
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Confirm the vehicle is VATS/PASS-Key-equipped with a resistor pellet key before proceeding, since this test does not apply to Passlock vehicles • 2. Remove the key and measure the pellet's resistance with an ohmmeter • 3. Compare the reading against the value the PCM/BCM expects for this vehicle • 4. Clean the decoder-ring contacts inside the ignition lock cylinder • 5. Have a correctly coded replacement key pellet cut if the resistance is wrong or unstable • 6. Test-start the vehicle to confirm the fuel-enable signal is restored

repair_fixes.title: Diagnose the Passlock lock-cylinder sensor circuit (Passlock-equipped vehicles only)
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Confirm the vehicle is Passlock/PASS-Key III-equipped with a plain or transponder key and no pellet before proceeding, since this test does not apply to VATS vehicles • 2. Backprobe the Passlock sensor signal wire at the BCM connector with a digital multimeter • 3. Sweep the voltage while slowly rotating the key from OFF to RUN and watch for a smooth reading versus an erratic one • 4. Inspect the sensor's connector and wiring for corrosion or a poor ground • 5. Replace the lock-cylinder sensor or housing if the signal is erratic, flat, or absent • 6. Run the manufacturer relearn procedure after replacement and confirm normal starting

repair_fixes.title: Repair theft-deterrent wiring or replace the BCM/security module
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Trace the theft-deterrent harness between the ignition lock, BCM, and PCM for chafed insulation or a corroded splice • 2. Repair any damaged wiring and recheck for a stable signal with a scan tool • 3. Confirm the key pellet, decoder ring, or Passlock sensor all test within specification before condemning the module • 4. Replace the BCM or theft-deterrent module if the wiring and sensor both check out • 5. Program the replacement module and relearn all working keys • 6. Verify normal starting across several ignition cycles and confirm no theft-deterrent codes return

repair_fixes.title: Check the module's dedicated fuse and battery/ground connections
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Identify the fuse feeding the specific powertrain module or sensor node named in the code • 2. Inspect the fuse and the engine-bay ground strap for corrosion • 3. Replace the fuse if blown and retest for communication

repair_fixes.title: Inspect and clean the engine-harness connector at the named module
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Locate the connector for the module or sensor identified in the fault description • 2. Inspect for melted plastic, oil contamination, or backed-out terminals • 3. Clean contacts with electrical contact cleaner and apply dielectric grease on reassembly • 4. Clear codes and confirm the module rejoins the network

repair_fixes.title: Repair the LIN/CAN sub-bus wiring feeding the module
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Trace the sub-bus wire from the named module toward the gateway connection point • 2. Inspect for chafe against exhaust heat shields or engine mount brackets • 3. Cut out and splice in heat-resistant wire rated for engine-bay temperatures • 4. Protect the repair with high-temperature adhesive-lined heat-shrink • 5. Verify the module reports live data on a scan tool

repair_fixes.title: Replace and reprogram the powertrain module or sensor node
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Confirm the module or smart sensor's internal transceiver has failed through isolation testing • 2. Remove and replace the component • 3. Program or configure the replacement using a factory-level scan tool where required • 4. Confirm stable communication and correct live data over a full drive cycle

repair_fixes.title: Inspect DPF differential pressure sensor hoses for cracks or swapped routing
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Locate the two pressure sensor hoses running to ports ahead of and behind the DPF • 2. Check for melted, kinked, or disconnected hose sections along the exhaust heat shield • 3. Confirm the hoses are routed to the correct ports and not swapped • 4. Reseat the hoses, clear the code, and monitor for its return

repair_fixes.title: Perform a manual DPF regeneration and inspect soot loading
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Connect a scan tool and check the current soot load percentage and DPF status PIDs • 2. Drive at sustained highway speed or command a parked regeneration per the platform procedure • 3. Confirm exhaust back-pressure and soot load fall to the normal range afterward • 4. Recheck efficiency monitor completion

repair_fixes.title: Send the DPF out for professional cleaning (ash removal)
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Remove the DPF assembly for inspection outside the vehicle • 2. Deliver it to a DPF cleaning service for pneumatic/thermal ash removal • 3. Weigh or pressure-test the cleaned filter against manufacturer specification before reinstalling • 4. Reinstall with new gaskets and clear the efficiency code

repair_fixes.title: Replace the diesel particulate filter assembly
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Confirm the filter substrate is physically cracked, melted, or missing via borescope or removal inspection • 2. Remove the DPF housing from the exhaust system, supporting adjacent flex joints • 3. Install the new filter with new gaskets and clamps, torquing to specification • 4. Clear codes and complete the DPF learn/reset procedure required by the platform

repair_fixes.title: Smoke-test intake for vacuum/air leaks
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Connect a smoke machine to the intake at idle • 2. Watch for smoke escaping at intake gaskets, PCV hoses, or brake booster line • 3. Replace any leaking gasket or hose • 4. Clear codes and verify fuel trims return toward 0%

repair_fixes.title: Replace fuel filter and test fuel pump output
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Replace the fuel filter if serviceable • 2. Measure fuel pump pressure and volume against spec under load • 3. Replace a weak pump if it fails the test • 4. Clear codes and confirm rail pressure holds steady

repair_fixes.steps: 1. Perform a fuel injector leak-down/drip test • 2. Identify any injector leaking past its seat • 3. Replace the faulty injector(s) and seals • 4. Clear codes and verify trims return toward 0%

repair_fixes.title: Replace stuck-open fuel pressure regulator
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Depressurize the fuel system • 2. Remove the regulator and inspect the diaphragm/valve for sticking • 3. Install the replacement regulator with new seals • 4. Clear codes and confirm rail pressure holds at commanded target

repair_fixes.title: Clean throttle bore and plate of carbon buildup
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Remove the intake ducting to access the throttle body plate • 2. Spray dedicated throttle body cleaner on the plate and bore with the plate held slightly open • 3. Wipe away loosened carbon with a lint-free cloth, avoiding the throttle position sensor end • 4. Reinstall ducting and perform a throttle relearn if the platform requires one

repair_fixes.title: Replace electronic throttle body/actuator motor assembly
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Disconnect the battery and unplug the throttle body electrical connector • 2. Remove the mounting bolts and lift off the throttle body with its gasket • 3. Install the replacement throttle body with a new gasket and torque bolts evenly • 4. Reconnect the battery and perform the required throttle/idle relearn procedure

repair_fixes.title: Repair throttle motor control circuit wiring
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Back-probe the throttle body connector and measure motor drive legs against the wiring diagram • 2. Trace the harness for a chafe point or corrosion between the throttle body and ECM • 3. Repair the damaged section with solder and heat-shrink • 4. Clear the code and confirm smooth throttle response through its full range

repair_fixes.title: Clean and reseat corroded throttle body connector
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Unplug the throttle body connector and inspect for corrosion or bent pins • 2. Clean contacts with electrical contact cleaner • 3. Apply dielectric grease and reseat the connector fully • 4. Clear the code and confirm it stays clear through a drive cycle

repair_fixes.title: Inspect and clean throttle/pedal position sensor connector
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Locate the throttle body or accelerator pedal assembly connector • 2. Unplug and inspect for corrosion or bent pins • 3. Clean contacts and reseat firmly • 4. Clear codes and verify smooth voltage sweep

repair_fixes.title: Replace throttle body or pedal position sensor assembly
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Unplug the connector and remove the mounting fasteners • 2. Install the replacement throttle body or pedal assembly • 3. Reconnect and perform a throttle relearn if required • 4. Clear codes and verify all channels track together

repair_fixes.title: Repair throttle/pedal position sensor wiring
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Back-probe the reference, signal, and ground circuits at the connector • 2. Voltage-drop test each leg back to the ECM • 3. Repair chafed conductors with heat-shrink splices • 4. Confirm all sensor channels agree throughout the pedal/throttle sweep

repair_fixes.title: Inspect and clean throttle/pedal position sensor connector
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Locate the throttle body or accelerator pedal assembly connector • 2. Unplug and inspect for corrosion or bent pins • 3. Clean contacts and reseat firmly • 4. Clear codes and verify smooth voltage sweep

repair_fixes.title: Replace throttle body or pedal position sensor assembly
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Unplug the connector and remove the mounting fasteners • 2. Install the replacement throttle body or pedal assembly • 3. Reconnect and perform a throttle relearn if required • 4. Clear codes and verify all channels track together

repair_fixes.title: Repair throttle/pedal position sensor wiring

repair_fixes.title: Check coolant level and inspect for external leaks
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Check coolant level cold and top off to spec • 2. Inspect hoses, radiator, and water pump weep hole for leaks • 3. Repair any obvious external leak source • 4. Clear codes and monitor warm-up time

repair_fixes.title: Replace stuck-open thermostat
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Drain coolant below the thermostat housing • 2. Remove the housing and replace the thermostat and gasket • 3. Refill coolant and bleed air from the system • 4. Confirm engine reaches operating temperature within expected time

repair_fixes.title: Replace failing water pump
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Drain coolant and remove drive components to access the water pump • 2. Remove the worn pump and inspect the impeller and bearing • 3. Install the replacement pump with a new gasket • 4. Refill, bleed, and verify stable circulation and temperature

repair_fixes.title: Smoke-test intake for vacuum/air leaks

repair_fixes.title: Inspect and repair exhaust manifold gasket leak
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Inspect the exhaust manifold gasket and studs near the upstream O2 sensor for leaks • 2. Replace the gasket and any corroded studs • 3. Torque to spec in sequence • 4. Clear codes and re-verify trim correction

repair_fixes.title: Inspect for exhaust leaks near the O2 sensor
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Inspect the exhaust manifold and pipe joints near the sensor bung for leaks • 2. Listen and smoke-test for exhaust leaks upstream of the sensor • 3. Replace gaskets or tighten fasteners as needed • 4. Clear codes and monitor sensor voltage trace

repair_fixes.title: Replace oxygen sensor
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Identify the affected bank/sensor position • 2. Remove the sensor with an O2 sensor socket • 3. Apply anti-seize to threads (avoid the tip) and install the new sensor • 4. Clear codes and confirm a normal switching voltage trace

repair_fixes.title: Repair O2 sensor signal circuit wiring
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Back-probe the signal and ground at the connector with the engine running • 2. Voltage-drop test the circuit back to the ECM • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring near the exhaust with high-temp splices • 4. Confirm proper switching activity

repair_fixes.title: Inspect for exhaust leaks near the O2 sensor
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Inspect the exhaust manifold and pipe joints near the sensor bung for leaks • 2. Listen and smoke-test for exhaust leaks upstream of the sensor • 3. Replace gaskets or tighten fasteners as needed • 4. Clear codes and monitor sensor voltage trace

repair_fixes.title: Replace oxygen sensor
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Identify the affected bank/sensor position • 2. Remove the sensor with an O2 sensor socket • 3. Apply anti-seize to threads (avoid the tip) and install the new sensor • 4. Clear codes and confirm a normal switching voltage trace

repair_fixes.title: Repair O2 sensor signal circuit wiring
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Back-probe the signal and ground at the connector with the engine running • 2. Voltage-drop test the circuit back to the ECM • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring near the exhaust with high-temp splices • 4. Confirm proper switching activity

repair_fixes.title: Check HV battery state of charge
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Verify the HV system is de-energized and locked out per the manufacturer's procedure before any inspection • 2. Read HV battery state of charge on a scan tool • 3. Charge the pack to a normal operating range if low • 4. Clear the code and recheck bus voltage at a normal state of charge

repair_fixes.title: Inspect main HV contactors for full seating
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Verify the HV system is de-energized and locked out per the manufacturer's procedure, then confirm zero volts with a rated meter • 2. Inspect the main positive/negative contactors for feedback confirming full seating • 3. Test contactor operation per the manufacturer's procedure • 4. Repair or replace a contactor found not seating fully

repair_fixes.title: Test HV bus voltage-sense circuit
repair_fixes.steps: 1. Verify the HV system is de-energized and locked out per the manufacturer's procedure, then confirm zero volts with a rated meter • 2. Inspect the bus voltage-sense wiring and connectors for damage or corrosion • 3. Repair or replace the sense circuit as needed • 4. Restore the HV system per procedure and clear the code • 5. Confirm bus voltage reads correctly across a drive cycle

repair_fixes.title: Check the module's dedicated fuse and battery/ground connections

recalls.summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2020-2021 Civic, 2020-2023 Ridgeline, 2021-2023 Passport, 2021-2022 Pilot, and 2020 Acura MDX vehicles.  The tie rod fastener that connects the brake booster and the brake master cylinder may have been improperly assembled during manufacturing, which can cause the brake master cylinder to separate from the booster assembly.
recalls.consequence: Brake master cylinder separation can cause a loss of brake function and increase the risk of a crash.
recalls.remedy: Dealers will inspect and repair the brake booster assembly as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed August 7, 2023.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are VEU, AEV, and ZET.

recalls.summary: Hyundai Motor America (Hyundai) is recalling certain 2019-2020 Elantra, 2019-2021 Kona and Veloster vehicles equipped with 2.0L Nu MPI engines.  The piston oil rings may not have been properly heat-treated, which could result in engine damage.
recalls.consequence: A damaged engine may stall, increasing the risk of a crash.  In addition, oil may leak onto hot exhaust components, increasing the risk of a fire.
recalls.remedy: Dealers will inspect and, if necessary, replace the engine, free of charge.  In addition, Hyundai will deploy Piston Ring Noise Sensing System (PNSS) software.  Owner notification letters were mailed August 24, 2021.  Owners may contact Hyundai customer service at 1-855-371-9460.

recalls.summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2019-2020 Acura MDX, MDX Sport Hybrid, RDX, TLX, Honda Accord, Civic Hatchback, Insight, 2019 Acura ILX, Honda Accord Hybrid, Civic Coupe, Civic Coupe Si, Civic Sedan, Civic Sedan Si, Civic Type R, Fit, HR-V, Odyssey, Passport, Pilot and Ridgeline, and 2018-2019 CR-V vehicles.  The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
recalls.consequence: Fuel pump failure can cause an engine stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
recalls.remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will replace the fuel pump assembly, free of charge.  Owner letters were mailed May 18, 2021.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Note: This recall is an expansion of recall 20V-314.

recalls.summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2021, 2023 Acura TLX, 2019-2024 RDX, 2017-2020, 2022-2026 MDX, 2017-2021, 2023, 2025 Honda Ridgeline, 2017-2022 Pilot, 2019-2021 Passport, 2018-2026 Odyssey, 2019-2022 Insight, 2019-2021 HR-V, 2018-2020 Fit, 2020-2022 CR-V Hybrid, 2017-2022 CR-V, 2017-2018, 2021 Civic Type R, 2017-2021 Civic hatchback, 2016-2020 Civic coupe, 2016-2022 Civic, 2017-2022 Accord Hybrid, and 2016-2022 Accord vehicles. The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit, which can cause the air bags to deploy unintentionally during a crash.
recalls.consequence: Air bags that deploy unintentionally during a crash increase the risk of injury.
recalls.remedy: Dealers will replace the seat weight sensors, free of charge. Owner notification letters were mailed July 7, 2026. Owners may contact Honda's customer service at 1-888-234-2138. Honda's numbers for this recall are BOL, WO9, OOA, WOM, XOH, NOC, POD, BOE, UOF, POB, EOG, AOI, QO8, TOJ, DO7, and SOK. This recall expands previous NHTSA recall number 24V064. Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs) involved in this recall will be searchable on NHTSA.gov beginning May 29, 2026.

recalls.summary: Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing (Toyota) is recalling certain 2020-2021 Avalon, Avalon Hybrid, Corolla, Highlander, Highlander Hybrid, RAV4, RAV4 Hybrid, Lexus ES350, Lexus RX350, Lexus RX450H, 2021 Sienna Hybrid, Lexus ES250, 2020-2022 Camry, Camry Hybrid, and ES300H vehicles.  A short circuit may develop in the Occupant Classification System (OCS) sensor, preventing the front passenger air bag from deploying.
recalls.consequence: An air bag that does not deploy during a crash increases the risk of injury.
recalls.remedy: Dealers will inspect and replace the sensor as necessary, free of charge.  Interim letters notifying owners of the safety risk were mailed in February 2024. Some final remedy owner letters were mailed October 31, 2024. Letters will continue to be mailed in phases through January 2026. Owners may contact Toyota customer service at 1-800-331-4331.  Toyota's number for this recall is 23TB15/23TA15 Lexus 23LB03/23LA03.

The fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.

recalls.remedy: Dealers will replace the fuel pump module, free of charge.  Owner letters were mailed September 6, 2024.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138. recalls.summary: Hyundai Motor America (Hyundai) is recalling certain 2019 Ioniq Hybrid and 2020 Elantra vehicles.  The right-side rear wheel lug nuts may have been insufficiently tightened, allowing the wheel to detach from the vehicle.
recalls.consequence: A wheel detaching from the vehicle increases the risk of a crash.
recalls.remedy: Hyundai will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and, if necessary, tighten the lug nuts, free of charge.  The recall began November 15, 2019.  Owners may contact Hyundai customer service at 1-800-251-0871.  Hyundai's number for this recall is 184.

recalls.summary: Hyundai Motor America (Hyundai) is recalling certain 2020 Elantra vehicles.  The lower control arm ball joint fasteners may have been insufficiently tightened allowing the ball joint to detach from the lower control arm.
recalls.consequence: A detached ball joint can cause a loss of vehicle control, increasing the risk of a crash.
recalls.remedy: Hyundai will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and, as necessary, tighten the ball joint fasteners, free of charge.  The recall began November 20, 2019.  Owners may contact Hyundai customer service at 1-855-371-9460.  Hyundai's number for this recall is 185.

recalls.summary: Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing (Toyota) is recalling certain 2020 Toyota Avalon Hybrid, Camry, Camry Hybrid and  Lexus ES300h and 2019-2020 RAV4 and RAV4 Hybrid vehicles equipped with 2.5L 4-Cylinder engines.  Porosity in the engine castings may result in cracks than can allow coolant to leak internally and/or externally.
recalls.consequence: A coolant leak can cause the engine to overheat and cause a vehicle stall in conventional gasoline vehicles, increasing the risk of a crash. Additionally, for all involved vehicles, the engine may get damaged mechanically, possibly resulting in an engine oil leak, increasing the risk of a fire.
recalls.remedy: Toyota will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and replace the engine including the engine block, as necessary, free of charge.  The recall began April 3, 2020.  Owners may contact Toyota customer service at 1-888-270-9371 or Lexus at 1-800-255-3987.  Toyota's number for this recall is 20TA04.  Lexus' number for this recall is 20LA02.

complaints.summary: The wheel becomes sticky/ jerky when driving at speeds over 40 mph and causes overcorrecting. It is worse around bends and makes holding the wheel straight difficult. The stickness is consistently present when on the highways making it incredibly dangerous to drive at these higher speeds as I am constantly having to overcorrect the wheel.   The dealer and an independent service center have both said they have been able to reproduce the sticky steering and that it is the steering rack. There is not any warning on my dashboard to indicate this part is failing which is also problematic as I should be made aware before my steering wheel completely freezes when driving at high speeds.

My 2020 Honda Civic experienced engine overheating and a cylinder 3 misfire (P0303). Two independent mechanics diagnosed a blown head gasket with coolant leaking into cylinder 3. The vehicle underwent a head gasket repair under Honda’s extended warranty. Less than a week after the repair, the engine overheated again while I was driving. I pulled over, waited approximately an hour for the engine to cool, added coolant, and drove to the dealership. The dealership later reported that the cylinder head was cracked near cylinder 4, close to the exhaust valve. When I picked my car up from the dealership, I scanned the vehicle and found the P0303 cylinder 3 misfire code. I am concerned that the engine may have an unresolved problem that could cause it to overheat again, sustain further damage, or lose power while driving. The vehicle is still in my possession and available for inspection. I have an appointment with an independent mechanic on October 24, 2026, to have the engine and cooling system inspected and determine what may have caused the repeated overheating. I am submitting this complaint to bring attention to a potential engine or engine-cooling safety defect and ask NHTSA to consider whether similar problems may be affecting other vehicles.

While fixing another problem, I pulled the codes from the ECM and found several P0087 (low fuel rail pressure).  The problem was apparently intermittent and if the engine service light came on, it was transient and the light cleared. So neither my wife or I noticed an engine service light.  I did some research and found that Denso found and reported a problem with the in tank fuel pump design to the NTSB in Feb. of 2020. We purchased the Camry in Dec. 2019 which meant we had the defective fuel pump.  I ordered a new Denso fuel pump and install it and no new codes have appeared in the ECM log.   Apparently Toyota has been slowly adding more years to the recall, but hasn't yet added the 2020 model year.  This is a problem since a number of people have reported engine stalls due to the defective fuel pump.  We live in the mountains, that might have been very dangerous especially if my wife suddenly lost power brakes and steering on a mountain road.  Why hasn't a recall been ordered for this pump on all effected years?

I am writing to file a complaint regarding the air conditioning system failure in my 2020 Honda Civic Sport. I took the vehicle to a mechanic for inspection, I was informed that the evaporator has failed and needs to be replaced. While researching this issue, I discovered that many other Honda Civic owners have reported similar air conditioning problems involving the evaporator and AC system. I also became aware of a 2021 letter involving American Honda Motor Co. and Honda dealership personnel regarding evaporator leaks in vehicles with VIN numbers beginning with 2HG or 19X. The letter stated that Honda was researching these vehicles in an effort to better understand the issue. Given the number of similar complaints and Honda’s apparent awareness and investigation into evaporator leaks, this appears to be a potentially widespread defect affecting these vehicles, even when properly maintained. The failure of the air conditioning system has caused significant inconvenience, medical issues and financial burden. I have severe Hyperthyroidism, and reside in CA. Due to extremely hot weather & no A/C, the heat affected my heart rate and health severely. My honda is utilized daily for employment & commitments. Without proper air conditioning in almost 3 years now, while driving my car, I was admitted into the hospital last summer 2026 for 5 days due to the extreme heat affecting my heart and almost causing me to go into a coma aka [thyroid storm]. I believe this issue should be investigated further, as it may indicate a defect in the vehicle’s air conditioning system. I respectfully request that the NHTSA review this matter and investigate whether the evaporator failure in the 2020 Honda Civic Sport is a recurring manufacturing defect that may warrant further action or assistance for affected vehicle owners. Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

The turbocharger bypass control solenoid valve circuit on my 2020 Civic Si has developed an intermittent open, setting DTC P0035. I diagnosed it myself: the solenoid coil measures 45 ohms and functions when commanded via bi-directional scan tool, and supply voltage is present at the harness connector. However, the control circuit reads approximately 9V in the off state when it should be near ground, and the reading fluctuates when the harness is flexed near the connector — indicating a partial break in the wiring consistent with vibration fatigue.  This is a safety concern because the ECM fault cascades to other systems. My scan report shows U0401-68 in the ABS module and U0416-68 in both the EPS and Integrated Driver Assistance modules. The result is that VSA stability control is disabled. I first noticed the problem because warning lights appear during hard cornering — precisely when stability control is most needed.  Honda has acknowledged this exact failure mode. Service Bulletin 18-044 (NHTSA ID 10142655), issued June 2018, covers the 2017 Civic Type R for DTC P0035 and states the cause as: heat and the natural frequency of the harness cause the coupler wire to oscillate, producing an open circuit to the turbocharger bypass control solenoid valve. The remedy was a replacement engine wire harness kit. The Si shares the same L15B7 engine family and the same bypass control solenoid circuit, but no campaign covers it. Owner forums document numerous P0035 wiring failures on non-Type-R 1.5T Civics.  I am requesting that NHTSA consider whether this defect and its effect on stability control warrants a safety investigation and expansion of the existing remedy to other 1.5T Civic models.
